title: Ex 3.4 #10 · Digit permutations alternating even and odd
prompt: A permutation of the ten digits 0, 1, 2, …, 9 lists each digit exactly once (it may start with 0). How many of these permutations alternate between even and odd digits, like 0123456789 or 9078563412?
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4, 10!/7! or binom(10, 3). P(n, k) and C(n, k) work too.

mistakes.hint: That fixes which kind of digit comes first. An alternating permutation can start with an even digit or with an odd one.
That counts every permutation of the digits, alternating or not.
Both the even digits and the odd digits can be shuffled among their own positions.

hints: First decide the pattern: even, odd, even, … or odd, even, odd, ….
Once the pattern is fixed, the five even digits fill the even slots in some order, and the five odd digits fill the odd slots.
solution: There are 2 patterns: start with an even digit or start with an odd digit.
For either pattern, the five even digits fill their five positions in $5! = 120$ ways and the five odd digits fill theirs in $5! = 120$ ways.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses factorials and the multiplication principle (Section 3.4).
